rows.claim: buildRunPlan's environment does not carry HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1; an exported HOSTNAME reaches the child

tests.test: GM and two-player campaign QC runner > plans HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 for every implemented group whatever the shell exports
tests.assertion: with process.env.HOSTNAME = 'some-machine', every implemented group's { ...process.env, ...plan.environment }.HOSTNAME equals '127.0.0.1' (filter of mismatches toEqual [])
tests.red: Expected Array []; received 26 [group, "some-machine"] pairs (fixture-smoke, membership-smoke, evidence-smoke, smoke, authority-pack1, ...)

tests.test: GM and two-player campaign QC runner > registers the approved catalog and deterministic implemented plans
tests.assertion: the authority-recovery plan environment toEqual now includes HOSTNAME: 127.0.0.1
tests.red: - "HOSTNAME": "127.0.0.1" missing from the received environment (Expected - 1, Received + 0)

rows.boundaryProbe: admission: HOSTNAME=some-machine PORT=1 node server.js exits 1 with [mp-boot] invalid HOSTNAME "some-machine"; buildRunPlan child env HOSTNAME=some-machine

rows.claim: runPlan prints no port/PID line, resolves no PID, and has no typed error for a missing enumeration tool

tests.test: runPlan server announcement > prints one GM2P_SERVER line with the owned port and the PID that owns it
tests.setup: a node http server child listening on 127.0.0.1:<free port> (killed in afterEach); a node -e harness takes the real smoke plan, swaps the Playwright command for a child printing CHILD_HOSTNAME=<env HOSTNAME>, points MEKSTATION_E2E_PORT at the owner port, runs core.runPlan with HOSTNAME=some-machine in its env
tests.assertion: toEqual { exit: '0', announcements: [{ port, pid: owner.pid }], childHostname: '127.0.0.1', stderr: '' } and the runner PID differs from owner.pid
tests.red: received { announcements: [], childHostname: undefined, exit: undefined, stderr: "TypeError: core.runPlan is not a function" at [eval]:7:6 } (runPlan is module-private, core.cjs:322-328; no GM2P_SERVER line exists)

tests.test: runPlan server announcement > throws MachineSnapshotError when the process enumeration tool is missing
tests.setup: same harness with PATH emptied (every case-variant of the PATH key removed, PATH set to "")
tests.red: received error: undefined (the harness died on the same TypeError before any error could be typed)

rows.claim: lint:units passes a path that lints zero files and never enforces a perPath ceiling

tests.test: lint:units per-path gates > fails, and exits 1, when empty-path lints zero files
tests.assertion: stdout contains 'LINT_UNITS_PATH empty-path files=0 findings=0 ceiling=none FAIL', last line 'LINT_UNITS_FAIL 0/5', exit 1
tests.red: received "LINT_UNITS_PATH empty-path 0\nLINT_UNITS_PASS 0/5" (exit 0 measured by hand from a scratch directory before the test was written)

tests.test: lint:units per-path gates > fails, and exits 1, when no-such-path lints zero files
tests.assertion: same, for a path that does not exist

tests.test: lint:units per-path gates > fails, and exits 1, when a path exceeds its perPath ceiling under the total
tests.setup: a temp e2e/over-ceiling.ts with perPath.e2e + 1 (= 51) no-explicit-any findings; run with --path e2e and the recorded file total
tests.assertion: stdout contains 'LINT_UNITS_PATH e2e files=1 findings=51 ceiling=50 FAIL', last line 'LINT_UNITS_FAIL 51/<file total>', exit 1
tests.red: received "LINT_UNITS_PATH e2e 51\nLINT_UNITS_PASS 51/100" - 51 findings over the e2e ceiling of 50 pass because only the total (100) is compared

tests.test: lint:units per-path gates > holds every default path exactly at its recorded ceiling
tests.assertion: the real CLI in the repository root prints one LINT_UNITS_PATH <path> files=<n> findings=<n> ceiling=<n> PASS row per perPath key, findings equal to the recorded ceiling and files > 0; last line LINT_UNITS_PASS <total>/<total>
tests.red: received Object {} (the baseline prints LINT_UNITS_PATH <path> <findings> with no files count and only e2e and scripts)

tests.test: lint:units ceiling file > parses, and its ceiling is the sum of perPath
lint:units verdict > is PASS|FAIL at <n> findings against a ceiling of <n> (5 rows)
tests.assertion: evaluateLintUnits returns failures: [] on PASS and ["total <f>/<c>"] on FAIL
tests.red: the failures key is absent (e.g. at 101/100: Expected - 3 lines "failures": ["total 101/100"])
